newsitem.title: FRANCE: Saudi Arabia may seek 800-900,000 T barley - ONIC.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia may seek 800-900,000 T barley - ONIC.

text.p: Saudi Arabia is expected to tap world markets again for feed barley and may seek to import 800,000 to 900,000 tonnes, the head of France's grain office ONIC said on Wednesday.
Director general Alain Moulinier did not provide a date for a future tender but told a news conference its timing would largely determine the share of business the European Union may grab.
"Saudi Arabia may be back in the market for an estimated 800,000 to 900,000 tonnes of barley," Moulinier said.
Earlier, European grain exporters said they expected Saudi Arabia, the world's largest barley importer, to shop again for barley from mid-April.
Moulinier said he could not pinpoint a date for a tender, adding "This ranged from within a day to a much longer period."
Canada and the European Union were the countries most likely to do business with the Saudis.
But Canada, which had only sold half of its available export supplies, faced logistical problems and would be penalised if the Saudis came out too soon, Moulinier said.
"It is all about timing. Much hinges on when the Saudis will make their bids. If it happens very shortly, this will hinder Canada. But one month from now it won't," he said.
Michel Ferret, the head of ONIC's international affairs division, said the European Union, which had a bumper barley crop in 1996, was also well placed to supply the Saudis.

Within the EU, Spanish barley stood a good chance, he said. Free-market Spanish barley had become more competitive, which had led some exporters to bids for export licences at recent EU grain auctions.
In January Saudi Arabia bought 1.2 million tonnes of optional-origin barley for February and March delivery.
